notes:
A Bluetooth name of Quest, such as Quest 3S, is Meta Quest. It is not labeled Ray-Ban / Meta glasses and it does not beep. A Meta company ID or service FEB8 without that name can still match the glasses row.

Bluetooth channel and frequency are left blank. Android does not report the advertising channel. Wi-Fi channel and frequency stay. A Wi-Fi signal of 0 is treated as no reading. The log keeps the Bluetooth advertisement, up to 512 bytes, and manufacturer data is its own field. Signature candidates keep a full custom service UUID.

Named radios is its own row on the Settings list, after Alerts. Signatures lists every class, including an empty one. Filters add Two-way radios and Military. The two-way rows match published Bluetooth names and do not beep. Military has no signatures yet. Catalog 101 removes the Novatel row. Address 28:80:A2 stays on Inseego.

Microsoft Nearby Sharing names the device type and, when sharing is set to Everyone nearby, the computer name. Wi-Fi vendor tags name WPA, WMM, WPS, and the other standard tags. A WMM tag no longer reads as Microsoft.

Radio detail can show GitHub catalog request on an unmatched Bluetooth radio when the phone has a network that claims internet, the name looks like a factory model, and that name was heard on two addresses. The tap opens a GitHub draft in the browser. Nothing is sent before that tap.

Bundled language files are written for this version. Two-way radios, Military, and GitHub catalog request are among the lines added since 1.1.42.
